subject: Scoring units, multipass rerank, and discount path — rate card clarifications
messages:
From: Kate Monroe <kate.monroe@findium.ai>
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@findium.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick: how are "scoring units" billed for multipass rerank?

Hi Sergio,

We loved the demo yesterday — nice job on the latency numbers. Our eng and procurement teams are trying to map your rate card to our cost model and one point is tripping us up: how do you count "scoring units" for a multipass rerank flow?

A concrete example: user search returns 100 candidates, first-pass model scores them, then a second re-ranking stage scores the top 20. Does Redwood bill 120 scoring units (100 + 20) or only 20 because you charge for the final pass? Also curious if classifier calls on items (e.g., spam filter) are priced the same way.

Can you share a short worked example and any guidance on packaging/discounts for sustained volume? We're close to issuing an RFP and want to avoid surprises.

Thanks,
Kate Monroe
Head of Search — Findium
attachments: --Findium_Rerank_Specs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Kate Monroe <kate.monroe@findium.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: how are "scoring units" billed for multipass rerank?

Hi Kate — great question, and thanks for the context. Short answer: we bill per scored candidate across all inference calls unless you opt into an endpoint configuration that consolidates pass accounting (more on that below). Long answer + worked example attached.

Worked example (default behavior):
- First-pass scoring: 100 candidates @ 1 score-unit each = 100 score units
- Second-pass rerank: top 20 candidates @ 1 score-unit each = 20 score units
- Classifier (spam flag) called only on top 20 = 20 classifier calls
- Total billed score units = 140 (we treat classifier calls as separate classifier-unit line item when using the classifier endpoint)

Key nuances:
- If you use our Relevance endpoint with multipass enabled and enable internal "consolidated accounting", we can map multi-stage scoring on the same request to a single logical scored-item if the additional passes are treated as refinements rather than full new inferences. That path typically requires a dedicated configuration and adds a small per-request surcharge but can reduce per-unit counts for large multipass pipelines.
- Batching matters: if you send the 100 candidates as a batched request vs 100 separate requests, throughput and effective cost-per-token change. Scoring unit pricing is orthogonal to token pricing — scoring units apply per candidate evaluated, token usage still billed for model compute.

I've attached a short table in the PDF showing baseline list prices and a sample invoice row. If you want, we can run your example in a sandbox to give a projected monthly invoice for your 2M queries/month estimate.

Would you like me to loop in pricing for a committed monthly volume vs on-demand? If yes, send the approx monthly calls and any preferred commit term.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
attachments: --Redwood_Ratecard_Q4_v3.pdf (rate card, 180KB)

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick: how are "scoring units" billed for multipass rerank?

Sergio / Marissa — FYI from Kate. Two quick internal notes:
1) Baseline public rate for score unit: $0.0009 per score-unit for hosted API (classifier calls billed at same per-unit in default config).
2) Consolidated accounting (consolidate multipass into logical items) is a product-ops toggle; recommend offering to Findium as a 5% uplift to baseline and then layer a volume discount.

If we do a 12-month commit at 2M queries/month (approx 70M scored items/month assuming 35 candidates avg), I propose: 18% off list score-unit, 10% off token spend, enterprise support included. Need Marissa to confirm margins and approve.

—Aditya

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick: how are "scoring units" billed for multipass rerank?

Thanks Aditya — margin check: with consolidated accounting enabled and the proposed uplift, blended unit economics still within target for 12-month commit at 2M queries/mo. Approve for commercial proposal with the following guardrails:
- Min commit 12 months, quarterly usage reviews
- 60-day onboarding credit of $10k to cover sandbox testing and evals
- Standard SLA for Dedicated not required (they want hosted) — include enhanced logging add-on as optional

Sergio: you can present the proposal but call out that classifier-heavy workloads (if they run classifier on all 100 candidates) will materially increase cost; recommend Findium restrict classifier to the top N or use a lightweight filter model.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Kate Monroe <kate.monroe@findium.ai>, procurement@findium.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial proposal: scoring accounting and volume path (summary)

Hi Kate — following internal review, here's a short summary to put on your RFP:

Option A — On-demand hosted (no consolidated accounting):
- Score unit list: $0.0009 / score-unit
- Classifier call: $0.0009 / classifier-unit
- Multipass billing: every inference call counts (e.g., 100 + 20 = 120 scoring units + classifier units as applicable)
- No minimum commitment; standard rate card applies

Option B — Committed volume + consolidated accounting (recommended for Findium):
- Baseline uplift for consolidated accounting: +5% to per-request surcharge (applied as $0.000045 per request in addition to unit billing)
- Proposed discount: 18% off score-unit + 10% off token compute for 12-month commit at >= 2M queries/month
- 60-day onboarding credit $10k; optional enhanced logging add-on $750/mo

Notes and recommended architectural changes:
- If you want to avoid double-counting, consider moving classifier to a lightweight pre-filter or using our cached prefix scores for cold-start candidates.
- We can enable a sandbox run for one week to produce an expected invoice under both options.

Next steps:
1) If the above looks ok, I will send a short SOW + commercial term sheet and a sandbox invite.
2) Procurement can share the RFP template and desired award cadence and we'll respond with final terms.

Best,
Sergio
Redwood Inference

- We want to run the one-week sandbox but need your PO/contract stub for procurement. Can you send an updated SOW and a short sandbox agreement?

If you can get those three items over this week, we'll prioritize Redwood in our procurement review.

Thanks,
Kate
